instruction: I was editing master slides but now I want to go back to editing my presentation content. Please return to Normal view so I can edit individual slides.

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(5); pyautogui.press('esc'); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('f10'); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('right', presses=2, interval=0.1); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('down', presses=2, interval=0.1); pyautogui.press('enter'); time.sleep(1)

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to return to Normal view from Master Slide view in LibreOffice Impress. Setup switches to Master view. Evaluator checks accessibility tree to confirm Normal view (Slides View panel visible, not in Master view).

llm_judge_reasons: The evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement (return to Normal view from Master view)
The metric uses appropriate dual verification: negative check for Master view (no 'Close Master View' menu item) and positive check for Normal view ('Slides View' panel visible)
The accessibility tree getter can extract the necessary UI state to distinguish between view modes
The logic will work correctly at runtime with proper XPath queries on the accessibility tree
The metric correctly does not access the 'expected' parameter, which is semantically acceptable for this boolean state check
Minor: The empty expected.rules dict is acceptable for a boolean check, though could be more explicit for self-documentation
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a more explicit expected structure for better self-documentation (e.g., {"expected_view": "normal"}), though this is not strictly necessary for correctness
